summary.intent: Fix Callisto's JS package publishing so the argv it builds works with each supported package manager, specifically yarn, and ship the fix as a PR stacked on the earlier Python fix PR.
summary.outcome: Verified against the real yarn, pnpm and bun CLIs that only yarn's `npm publish` rejects `--registry`. Fixed the argv builder in registry_argv.rs, extended its test, documented the behavior in docs/publishing.md, added a changeset, ran full CI and opened the PR (#376, stacked on #375).

repo: JS publish argvs are built in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs, with unit tests alongside.
The repo uses changesets, and a full CI run is part of the PR workflow.
PRs can be stacked: #376 was branched from the Python fix branch (#375) and carries its commit, so the two are linked and checked for overlap with #369 and #372.
docs/publishing.md has an npm section covering JS publishing, which is where yarn and registry behavior is documented.

code.finding: The publish argv assembly passed `--registry` to yarn, but yarn 4's `npm publish` supports only `--access` and `--tag`. bun (`--registry`, `--access`, `--tag`) and pnpm (`--registry`) accept the flags Callisto passes, so only the yarn path needed changing.

workflow: Check the real CLI's help output or behavior to confirm which flags it supports instead of assuming.
Run package-manager probes from a neutral directory. A directory that declares yarn as its package manager makes pnpm refuse to run.
Check a new branch's commits against main to see whether it inherited commits from the parent branch, then link and stack the PRs on purpose.

friction: pnpm refused to run in the probe directory because it declares yarn, so the probes had to be rerun from a neutral directory.
The new PR branch inherited the Python fix commit, which required checking and stacking the PRs.
open_items: #376 is stacked on #375, so it depends on that PR merging first.
Overlap with open PRs #369 and #372 was checked, but the transcript does not show the result.
